newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler idles 2,130 at transmission plant.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler idles 2,130 at transmission plant.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Monday it laid off 2,130 workers at its Kokomo, Ind., transmission plant because of the 12-day-old engine plant strike that has shut down a major portion of its North American truck production.

Chrysler spokesman Tony Cervone said the transmission plant workers were told not to report to work on Monday. The action raises the number of Chrysler workers idled by the strike to over 17,000 in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
The strike at Chrysler's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit has cut off supplies of V-6, V-8 and V-10 engines used in Chrysler's most popular light truck models.

Assembly plants shut down so far include the Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicle plant in Detroit; the Dodge City truck complex in Warren, Mich., which builds the Dodge Ram and Dakota pickups; Dodge Ram plants in Fenton, Mo., Lago Alberto and Saltillo, Mexico; and a plant that builds large vans in Windsor, Ontario.
Analysts have estimated that production losses are reducing Chrysler's profits by up to $20 million a day.

Cervone said no formal meetings were scheduled Monday by negotiators for the company and United Auto Workers Local 51. Talks remained largely dormant over the weekend, but top officials remain in contact by telephone.

The union wants Chrysler to drop plans to shift production of drive shafts from the Mound Road plant to an outside supplier as a condition of a new local labor contract for the plant. UAW officials say the outsourcing move would eliminate more than 200 jobs from the plant.
